I've been playing Halo since it was first released. Played them all in order since then. Some of my best gaming memories come from LANs where we threw a couple Xboxes together and played Halo:CE all night.

Favorite campaign mission? Tough call, but I would have to say Truth and Reconciliation as my number one. Followed closely by Silent Cartographer and Cairo Station.

(Rant incoming) tl;dr: didn't like 4, 60% I won't buy 5

As for Halo 5...I'm really on the fence about it. I don't play Halo for the multiplayer anymore and that seems to be all people talk about anymore (at least on other sites). Also the Halo 4 campaign just didn't feel right to me, it didn't really feel like Halo. I think part of that is due to 343i and the creative direction they've taken the game in. The overdone armor designs and the redesigned covenant just don't appeal to me. In my opinion they've thrown away the aesthetic of the original trilogy and gone in the wrong direction. On top of that the new enemies were incredibly unvaried which made the combat tedious and frustrating. Then an anti-climactic QTE boss "fight" to top it all off. Also what was up with the ChiefxCortana romance subplot? Why is that even a thing?

/rant

Anyway, feelings for 4 aside, I love everything about the Halo series, the lore, the atmosphere, the story, the gameplay, and most importantly the characters.

You've pretty summed up most of my feelings about Halo 4. The multiplayer got stale far quicker for me than any previous Halo title too. Giving people the ability to customize what weapons they spawn with killed my fervor for my favorite playlist, Big Team Battle, since anyone could spawn with a plasma pistol and plasma grenades to protect themselves from vehicles. It just made my job as the default driver hell-on-wheels.

After feeling betrayed by 343i during the MCC debacle Halo 5 is going to have to be something really special for me to want to buy it. Sadly it will be the first Halo game I haven't bought on launch day.

I've been playing since the very beginning. Picked up an Xbox on launch day with Halo bundled in, haven't put it down since.

Favorite campaign mission is definitely the Covenant on Halo 3, it's just got a little bit of everything, plus an epic battle against two scarabs at the end

I will be buying Halo 5, but not pre-ordering. I don't like the changes to multiplayer, so I will be getting it for the campaign

I first got into Halo just before Halo 2 launched, but wasn't allowed to play it until 2007. Of course I just went to my friends house and played it for over 3 years (actually bought his copy from him in secret so I could play at home).

My first game was Halo 2 and it's still my favorite. Favorite mission is definitely Outskirts closely followed Delta Halo. Will I buy Halo 5? Um, fuck yeah! I preordered it in 2014.

I've been playing Halo since the beginning. My next door neighbor and I would spend countless hours playing CE campaign split-screen. Halo 2 just about blew my mind. I can't even begin to estimate how much of my life I lost to that game. Honestly I don't think I can pick a single favorite campaign mission since they all have their great moments, but my favorite campaign by a landslide was Reach. That aesthetic and soundtrack gave me chills.

As far as Halo 5 goes, 343i is going to have to pull a miracle out of their ass to get me to buy it. The MCC should have been a Halo Renaissance for me, but instead it stabbed my enthusiasm for Halo right in the heart. I just ran out of patience waiting for them to get it stable and relatively lag free. If the Halo 5 campaign isn't absolutely amazing then it is a no-go for me. 343i failed to keep me interested in the multiplayer for 5's direct predecessor, Halo 4, and right now I am expecting more of the same for 5.

I've played Halo since late 2004. I was introduced to the game through the PC version of Halo: Combat Evolved. It was on sale for like $10; an amazing investment. Later that year I was introduced to Custom Edition. That spawned some of my favorite Online gaming moments.

I didn't buy a 360 until Halo: Reach came out.
